name: QPSK · CC K=7 · block 48×32 · CCSDS scrambler · CRC-16 · 12 dB
what: The full chain, decoded blind and proven.

name: Same recipe at 7 dB
what: Low SNR: the PHY tests lose power, the coding layer carries the proof.

name: Same recipe, a 0.66 s capture at 7 dB
what: Too short to decide the code: the Data-Sufficiency Engine says how many seconds to record.

name: QPSK · CC K=5 · block 24×64 · PRBS-9 · clock −12 ppm
what: A different code and interleaver geometry; the recorder's clock error is measured.

name: QPSK · CC K=7 · no interleaver · degree-6 scrambler
what: The scrambler is in no library; its polynomial and seed are solved blind.

name: QPSK · CC K=9 · no scrambler · 6.37 samples/symbol
what: Non-integer oversampling and a long code.

name: One emitter, three sensors (+1 decoy) · evidence stitching
what: Each capture is too short alone; pooled they decode, each is proven, and the decoy from another emitter is caught. Sensor clocks, tuning, gains and an inverted spectrum are measured.

name: Pure noise
what: Nothing to find: the answer must be 'undecided', never a fabricated recipe.

what: US military HF serial-tone modem; a 1.4 s burst.

what: Bursty PSK at 1800 Bd, 1440 Hz carrier.

name: PSK31 (HF amateur, BPSK 31.25 Bd)
what: A very narrow BPSK signal, about 60 Hz wide.
